color_palette.pigment_blue_deep: Deep cobalt/ultramarine blue — used for the central solar disk swirl field and the nymph/figure robes
color_palette.pigment_blue_pale: Pale blue-grey — used for the four diagonal arm/tube structures crossing the composition
color_palette.pigment_brown_ink: Brown/sepia ink — primary writing ink for all text (all loci)
color_palette.pigment_gold_yellow: Warm gold/ochre — used for the sun face glyph at center
color_palette.pigment_white_parchment: Natural vellum — background; uncoloured zones including text bands and corner cloud-fan forms
color_palette.pigment_blue_green_wash: Pale blue-green wash — faint tint on corner fan/cloud elements
color_palette.notes: Red ink is NOT present on this folio — all text is written in brown/sepia. This distinguishes f85r2 from cosmological folios such as f67r2 where red ink is dominant.

syntax_clues_detected: f85r2.1  is @Cc — CRITICAL: long text inscribed INSIDE or along the inner ring of the central medallion (concentric circle zone). 34 dot-separated words — the longest single @Cc inscription in this dataset.
f85r2.2–6  is @Pb/+Pb group 1 — paragraph block inscribed in the UPPER text band (above the central composition, between the two upper diagonal arms)
f85r2.7–11 is @Pb/+Pb group 2 — paragraph block inscribed in the LEFT text band (left of center, between the left arm and the left quadrant)
f85r2.12–17 is @Pb/+Pb group 3 — paragraph block inscribed in the LOWER text band (below the central medallion, between the two lower diagonal arms)
f85r2.18–23 is @Pb/+Pb group 4 — paragraph block inscribed in the RIGHT text band (right of center, between the right arm and right quadrant)
f85r2.24 is @Cc — second @Cc inscription inside the central medallion, shorter (13 words). Together f85r2.1 and f85r2.24 form the inner ring text of the central circle zone.
NO <-> bisection markers detected on any line

central_medallion.description: The dominant circular illustration at the geometric center of the folio. Outer boundary is a scalloped/lobed decorative ring. Interior filled with a deep cobalt blue painted swirling pattern (representing water, sky, or cosmos). At the absolute center sits the sun_face_glyph in gold/ochre. Four nymph figures are positioned at cardinal points on the inner ring's perimeter. The entire medallion is the anchor for both @Cc loci.
central_medallion.color: Outer ring: uncoloured parchment with brown ink; interior: deep cobalt blue with gold sun center

sun_face_glyph.description: A circular human face with radiating pointed spikes — a stylised sun symbol — at the absolute center of the central medallion. Drawn in warm gold/ochre pigment with brown ink detailing for the facial features. Surrounded by the deep cobalt blue swirl.
sun_face_glyph.color: Gold/ochre pigment face disc; brown ink line-work for spikes and facial features

blue_swirl_field.description: The large painted area of deep cobalt/ultramarine blue filling the interior of the central medallion around the sun face. The brushwork creates a swirling motion effect, with lighter and darker passages. This is the most intensely coloured element on the folio.
blue_swirl_field.color: Deep cobalt/ultramarine blue pigment; some areas show brushwork variation from deep to medium blue

inner_ring.description: A wide annular band of uncoloured parchment forming a ring between the blue swirl zone and the outer scalloped edge. This is the zone where both @Cc text blocks (f85r2.1 and f85r2.24) are inscribed. The ring has a scalloped outer edge and a relatively smooth inner edge touching the blue zone.
inner_ring.color: Uncoloured parchment; text in brown/sepia ink

nymph_figure_top.description: A seated female nymph figure positioned at the top of the inner ring, between the two upper diagonal arms where they converge on the medallion. She appears to be seated or crouching, facing inward toward the center. Rendered with a distinctly deep blue garment/robe — the most fully coloured of the four nymph figures.
nymph_figure_top.color: Deep cobalt blue robe/garment; pale parchment skin; brown ink line-work

nymph_figure_left.description: A standing or seated female nymph figure to the left of the inner ring, at approximately the 9 o'clock position. Faces inward. Rendered with deep blue garment, consistent with nymph_figure_top in colour application.
nymph_figure_left.color: Deep cobalt blue garment; parchment skin; brown ink line-work

nymph_figure_right.description: A smaller female nymph figure at the right of the inner ring (~3 o'clock position). Appears smaller in scale than the other figures. Partial blue colouring on garment, possibly less fully rendered.
nymph_figure_right.color: Partial cobalt blue on garment; otherwise parchment and brown ink

nymph_figure_bottom.description: A female nymph figure at the bottom of the inner ring (~6 o'clock position), depicted in an inverted or upward-facing orientation relative to the top figure. Lighter colouring — the blue garment is less intense or partially painted.
nymph_figure_bottom.color: Light cobalt blue wash on garment; parchment skin; brown ink line-work

diagonal_arm_NW_SE.description: One of two pairs of diagonal arms (tube or banner-like structures) crossing the composition diagonally. This pair runs from the upper-left to the lower-right, passing behind/through the central medallion zone. Painted in a pale blue-grey. Each arm terminates in one of the corner fan structures.
diagonal_arm_NW_SE.color: Pale blue-grey pigment wash; brown ink outlines

diagonal_arm_NE_SW.description: The second pair of diagonal arms crossing from upper-right to lower-left. Together with diagonal_arm_NW_SE they form an 'X' pattern centered on the medallion. Same pale blue-grey colouring.
diagonal_arm_NE_SW.color: Pale blue-grey pigment wash; brown ink outlines

corner_fan_NW.description: Upper-left corner decorative element — a fan or shell of overlapping curved parallel lines, like a stylised wing or cloud. Uncoloured or with a very faint pale wash. The lines are drawn in brown ink.
corner_fan_NW.color: Uncoloured parchment; faint pale blue-green wash on some layers; brown ink line-work

corner_fan_NE.description: Upper-right corner fan — similar form to corner_fan_NW. Slightly more visible pale blue-green wash compared to the left.
corner_fan_NE.color: Pale blue-green wash; brown ink line-work

corner_fan_SW.description: Lower-left corner fan. Uncoloured or faint wash only.
corner_fan_SW.color: Uncoloured parchment; faint pale wash; brown ink line-work

corner_fan_SE.description: Lower-right corner fan. Uncoloured or faint wash only.
corner_fan_SE.color: Uncoloured parchment; faint pale wash; brown ink line-work

upper_text_band.description: The open text zone in the upper quadrant of the composition — the roughly elliptical/lens-shaped space framed above by the folio top margin, left and right by the two upper diagonal arms, and below by the nymph_figure_top and the inner ring. Contains @Pb group 1 (f85r2.2–6). Text written in brown ink.

left_text_band.description: The arc-shaped text zone to the left of the central medallion, framed by the left pair of diagonal arms. Contains @Pb group 2 (f85r2.7–11). Text runs in roughly parallel horizontal lines following the available space.

lower_text_band.description: The text zone in the lower quadrant, framed by the two lower diagonal arms and below by the lower folio margin. Contains @Pb group 3 (f85r2.12–17). Text written in brown ink.

right_text_band.description: The arc-shaped text zone to the right of the central medallion, framed by the right diagonal arms. Contains @Pb group 4 (f85r2.18–23). Text runs in roughly parallel lines following the arc of available space.

rust_stain.description: A small brownish-orange pigment or rust stain at the top-center of the folio, above the nymph_figure_top and between the two upper diagonal arms. It does not obscure any text.
rust_stain.color: Rust-brown orange — likely an old pigment spatter or foxing spot

text_blocks_mapping.description: f85r2.1 @Cc — the primary inner ring inscription. This is a very long single-locus @Cc block (34 words) that runs continuously around the inner ring of the central medallion. The text spirals or arcs along the ring's inner circumference, written in brown ink against the uncoloured parchment of the inner_ring zone. It is the most extensive inscription on the folio.

lines.color: Brown/sepia ink on uncoloured parchment inner ring
lines.interaction: This @Cc inscription runs along the inner ring of the central_medallion. The text follows the arc of the ring, with individual words separated by dots. The inner boundary of the inscription field is the deep cobalt blue swirl zone; the outer boundary is the scalloped edge of the inner ring. The inscription appears to complete one full revolution (or more) around the ring, wrapping past the four nymph figures which create small text-free gaps. The nymph_figure_top causes a gap approximately at the 12 o'clock position (x≈400–500, y≈280–330). The nymph_figure_left causes a gap at 9 o'clock (x≈255–300, y≈450–510). The nymph_figure_right causes a gap at 3 o'clock (x≈630–680, y≈450–510). The nymph_figure_bottom causes a gap at 6 o'clock (x≈400–500, y≈640–700).

text_blocks_mapping.description: f85r2.2–6: @Pb group 1. Five lines inscribed in the upper_text_band — the open zone above the central medallion, framed by the two upper pale-blue diagonal arms. Text runs in roughly horizontal lines from left to right, written in brown ink. The lines are short to medium length, constrained by the narrowing space between the converging diagonal arms.

lines.interaction: First line of upper text band. Short — 5 words. The line is constrained by the pale-blue diagonal arms which form the left (NW arm) and right (NE arm) boundaries of this zone. Approximate left boundary from NW arm: x≈270. Approximate right boundary from NE arm: x≈600.
Second line. Slightly wider zone as the diagonal arms diverge moving downward.
Third line. Zone continues to widen.
Fourth line. Short — 3 words.
Fifth and final line of upper band. Single word — very short. Positioned centrally just above the nymph_figure_top. The zone narrows here as the arms approach the medallion.

text_blocks_mapping.description: f85r2.7–11: @Pb group 2. Five lines inscribed in the left_text_band — the arc-shaped open zone to the left of the central medallion, between the NW and SW diagonal arms. Text runs in roughly horizontal lines. Written in brown ink. Lines are medium length.

lines.interaction: First line of left text band. Runs along the upper portion of the left zone, bounded on the right by the pale-blue NW diagonal arm and on the left by the folio edge. The zone is arc-shaped — widest near the vertical midpoint.
Second line. Longer — 6 words.
Third line.
Fourth line.
Fifth and final line of left band. 'chotcog' is an unusual glyph sequence. The zone narrows toward the SW arm below this point.

text_blocks_mapping.description: f85r2.12–17: @Pb group 3. Six lines inscribed in the lower_text_band — the open zone below the central medallion, framed by the two lower diagonal arms and the nymph_figure_bottom. Text runs in roughly horizontal lines, written in brown ink.

lines.interaction: First line of lower text band. Short — 4 words. Positioned just below the nymph_figure_bottom. Zone constrained by the lower diagonal arms converging downward.
Second line. Zone slightly wider.
Third line.
Fourth line.
Fifth line. Contains 'an' — unusually short word/particle.
Sixth and final line of lower band. Short — 3 words. Lower text zone ends here; below this the diagonal arms and corner fans take over.

text_blocks_mapping.description: f85r2.18–23: @Pb group 4. Six lines inscribed in the right_text_band — the arc-shaped zone to the right of the central medallion, between the NE and SE diagonal arms. Text runs in roughly horizontal lines, written in brown ink. This is the longest @Pb group (6 lines, more words per line).

lines.interaction: First line of right text band. Positioned in the upper portion of the right zone. Bounded on the left by the pale-blue NE diagonal arm and on the right by the folio margin.
Second line.
Third line. Longer — 8 words. Widest zone in right band.
Fourth line.
Fifth line. Contains 'qose,eey' with a comma-separator — an unusual internal punctuation within a word token. Also 'og' at end — single short token.
Sixth and final line of right band. Zone narrows toward the SE arm below.

text_blocks_mapping.description: f85r2.24 @Cc — the second inner ring inscription, shorter than f85r2.1 (13 words). Positioned in a different arc sector of the inner ring from f85r2.1, completing or supplementing the ring inscription. Together with f85r2.1 they provide the full @Cc text of the central medallion's inner ring.

lines.color: Brown/sepia ink on uncoloured parchment inner ring
lines.interaction: Second @Cc arc inscription on the inner ring. Contains two comma-separated compound tokens: 'al,chedy' and 'air,ol' and 'ar,am' — suggesting a scribe's ligature or unusual glyph grouping. This block may occupy a different arc sector of the inner ring from f85r2.1, or may form an inner sub-ring. The bounding box covers the full ring zone; actual ink position is arc-constrained within it.

isolated_zones.description: The deep cobalt blue painted swirl occupying the interior of the central medallion is entirely text-free. No glyph is written over the blue pigment. The @Cc text is confined to the inner_ring zone which borders the blue zone but does not enter it. The gold sun face at center is also text-free.
The gold/ochre sun face at the absolute center is text-free. It is the visual focus of the entire composition. No text overlaps it.

isolated_zones.status: Text-free body — creates gap in @Cc inner ring inscription
isolated_zones.description: The nymph figure at the 12 o'clock position of the inner ring creates a text-free interruption in the @Cc inscription arc at approximately x=400–500, y=270–330. The text on the inner ring must navigate around her figure.

isolated_zones.description: Creates a text-free gap in the inner ring @Cc inscription at the 3 o'clock position.

isolated_zones.description: Creates a text-free gap in the inner ring @Cc inscription at the 6 o'clock position, and defines the upper boundary of the lower_text_band.

The pale blue diagonal arms are text-free throughout their length. They function purely as structural framing elements, defining the boundaries of the four text bands. No @Pb or @Cc text is inscribed on the arms themselves.
Same as NW_SE pair — text-free pale blue structure.
All four corner fans are text-free decorative elements. They occupy the extreme corners of the folio (x≈45–175, y≈48–215 for NW), filling the spaces left by the diagonal arms.
